1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (generated scaffold)](#project-structure-generated-scaffold)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
52	
53	## Project structure (generated scaffold)
54	
55	```
56	<ProjectName>/
57	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
58	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
59	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
60	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
61	├── operate.json            # runtime options
62	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
63	```
64	
65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
119	
120	Example — manual start trigger:
121	
122	```json
123	{
124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
191	
192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
227	
228	## Edge — both ports required
229	
230	```json
231	{
232	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
233	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
234	  "sourcePort": "output",
235	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
236	  "targetPort": "input"
237	}
238	```
239	
240	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
241	>
242	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.
245	
246	## Definition entry
247	
248	Every node type appearing in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`. Get the correct definition from:
249	
250	```bash
251	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
252	```
253	
254	Copy the returned node definition object into your `definitions` array. Depending on CLI/plugin version, that object may appear at `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`. Do not write definitions by hand — always pull from the registry to ensure schema compliance.
255	
256	## Common node types
257	
258	| Type | Purpose | Key inputs |
259	|------|---------|------------|
260	| `core.trigger.manual` | Entry point | `entryPointId` |
261	| `core.trigger.scheduled` | Recurring schedule trigger | `entryPointId`, `timerType`, `timerPreset` |
262	| `core.action.script` | Run JavaScript | `script` |
263	| `core.action.http.v2` | HTTP request | `method`, `url`, `headers`, `body` |
264	| `core.action.transform` | Map/filter/group data | `collection`, `operations` |
265	| `core.logic.decision` | If/else branch | `expression` |
266	| `core.logic.switch` | Multi-way branch | `cases` |
267	| `core.logic.loop` | Iterate collection | `collection`, `parallel` |
268	| `core.logic.merge` | Sync parallel paths | — |
269	| `core.control.end` | Graceful end | — |
270	| `core.logic.terminate` | Abort workflow | — |
271	
272	> The BPMN type for each node (e.g., `bpmn:StartEvent`, `bpmn:ScriptTask`) lives in the `definitions` entry copied from `uip maestro flow registry get`. Instances do not carry the BPMN type.
273	
274	For full details on each node (ports, inputs, outputs, when to use), see the [Author planning architecture guide](../author/references/planning-arch.md). For implementation resolution (registry lookups, connection binding, reference field resolution), see the [Author planning implementation guide](../author/references/planning-impl.md).
275	
276	Discover all available types:
277	```bash
278	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
279	uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>
280	```
281	
282	## Standard ports by node type
283	
284	| Node type | Source ports (outgoing) | Target ports (incoming) |
285	|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
286	| `core.trigger.manual` | `output` | — |
287	| `core.action.script` | `success`, `error` | `input` |
288	| `core.action.http.v2` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic) | `input` |
289	| `core.action.transform` | `output`, `error` | `input` |
290	| `core.logic.decision` | `true`, `false` | `input` |
291	| `core.logic.switch` | `case-{id}` (dynamic), `default` | `input` |
292	| `core.logic.loop` | `success`, `output` | `input`, `loopBack` |
293	| `core.logic.merge` | `output` | `input` |
294	| `core.control.end` | — | `input` |
295	| `core.logic.terminate` | — | `input` |
296	
297	Connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes follow the same pattern as the generic action nodes above: a primary source port plus an implicit `error` port.
298	
299	Verify exact ports for any node type:
300	```bash
301	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
302	# Look at Data.Node.handleConfiguration[].handles[].id
303	# Also check Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling — see "Implicit error port" below
304	```
305	
306	## Implicit error port on action nodes
307	
308	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
309	
310	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
311	
312	### Default: off — enable only for a failure the flow actually handles
313	
314	`inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is **opt-in, and stays off unless the requirements name a failure fallback.** Turning it on suppresses the node's fault: the node returns instead of faulting and execution continues. Enable it only when both hold:
315	
316	1. The requirements state what should happen when this node fails ("if the call fails, …", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts") — **and**
317	2. You wire the node's `error` port to a handler that produces an outcome distinguishable from success.
318	
319	Never set the flag on a node that has no outgoing `error` edge — it suppresses the fault with nothing to catch it, converting a real failure into a run that reports success. Let the CLI own the flag: `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set it from the error edges actually present. If you find the flag on a node with no error edge, remove it.
320	
321	### Do not swallow the failure
322	
323	An `error` edge must not rejoin the happy path. When it does, every failure walks the success route and the run reports `Completed` while the work never happened — the flow "always looks successful."
324	
325	| | Error-path target | Result |
326	| --- | --- | --- |
327	| ✗ | The next node on the happy path | Failure is invisible; downstream nodes run on missing data |
328	| ✗ | The same End node the success path reaches | Success path's output mappings run against the failed node's empty output |
329	| ✓ | A **distinct** End node mapping an error/status `out` variable | Caller can tell failure from success |
330	| ✓ | `core.logic.terminate` | Aborts the flow when recovery is impossible — see [terminate/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/terminate/impl.md) |
331	| ✓ | A recovery branch that rejoins **only after obtaining valid data** — a retry that succeeded, or a fallback source that returned data | Downstream runs on real data, not on the failed node's empty output |
332	
333	```text
334	Trigger -> HTTP Request
335	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
336	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", message from $vars.httpCall.error)
337	```
338	
339	### When the error port fires
340	
341	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
342	- Request timeouts
343	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
344	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
345	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
346	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
347	
348	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`. **That is the correct default, not a defect to design around** — a faulted run is visible to the operator; a swallowed failure is not. Only trade the fault for an error path when the requirements say what that path should do.
349	
350	### Wiring the error port
351	
352	```bash
353	# Confirm the node supports error handling
354	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
355	
356	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
357	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
358	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
359	```
360	
361	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically — only for nodes that have an error edge. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself **on those nodes only**:
362	
363	```json
364	{
365	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
366	  "inputs": {
367	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
368	  }
369	}
370	```
371	
372	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
373	
374	### Error port vs other branching
375	
376	| Mechanism | When to use |
377	| --- | --- |
378	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
379	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
380	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
381	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

502	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
503	
504	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). Preserve its lifecycle-generated contents; project scaffolding creates it, and the Flow lifecycle regenerates it before execution or publication.
505	
506	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
507	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
508	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
509	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
510	
511	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
512	
513	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
514	
515	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
516	
517	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
518	
519	```json
520	"bindings": [
521	  {
522	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
523	    "name": "name",
524	    "type": "string",
525	    "resource": "process",
526	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
527	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
528	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
529	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
530	  },
531	  {
532	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
533	    "name": "folderPath",
534	    "type": "string",
535	    "resource": "process",
536	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
537	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
538	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
539	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
540	  }
541	]
542	```
543	
544	**Rules:**
545	
546	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
547	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
548	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
549	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
550	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
551	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
552	
553	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
554	
555	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
556	
557	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
558	
559	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.

1	# Flow Editing Operations
2	
3	Strategy selection and shared concepts for modifying `.flow` files. Direct `.flow` authoring is required for non-carve-out structural edits; CLI is reserved for the documented product-managed configuration carve-outs.
4	
5	## Tool Selection Ladder
6	
7	> **Pick the lowest-numbered tool that fits the operation.** If no rung fits, stop and ask the user. Scripting languages (`python`, `node`, `jq`, `sed`, `awk`, shell heredocs) are a last resort and require explicit user approval — see rung 4.
8	>
9	> 1. **CLI-managed carve-outs only** → use the relevant plugin workflow for connector activity, connector-trigger, or managed HTTP operations when the CLI populates product-managed state (`inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, connection resources).
10	> 2. **Any structural `.flow` mutation** (add/delete OOTB nodes, add/delete edges, add/edit variables, in-place value tweaks, output mapping, subflows, scheduled triggers, non-connector resources, inline-agent node/wiring) → `Edit`.
11	> 3. **Wholesale file rewrite** (only when ≥70% of nodes change, e.g., scaffolding from a template) → `Write` — but never on a flow that already contains CLI-owned nodes (connector, connector-trigger, managed HTTP): the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` and `flow validate` won't catch it. Use `Edit` (rung 2); if you do `Write`, re-run `node configure` **as the last write** to touch `inputs.detail` / `bindings[]` (a later `Write` re-clobbers it). See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
12	> 4. **Anything else** → STOP and ask the user. A scripting language is a last resort: surface the trade-offs (state bypass, opaque diff, no interruption point) and present finite options — typically **Use `Edit` instead** / **Use `Write` (full rewrite)** / **Approve the script for this change** / **Cancel** / **Something else**. Only proceed after the user explicitly approves that path for this specific change. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md).
13	
14	### Why not Python / Node / jq / sed?
15	
16	- The CLI auto-manages cross-cutting state (`definitions[]`, `variables.nodes`, edge references, layout). A scripting mutation bypasses that and forces hand-rolling it — extra surface for mistakes.
17	- `Edit` shows a line-by-line diff in the transcript; a script is an opaque payload. The user reviews tool calls, not script bodies.
18	- `Edit` calls are atomic per-call. A coordinated multi-section change is *not* one transaction — it's a sequence of `Edit` calls the user can interrupt between. Treating it as a single Python script removes that interruption point.
19	
20	If the change feels too tangled for a sequence of `Edit` calls, use `Write` for the whole file or stop and ask the user (see rung 4 above) — see the `Edit`/`Write` recipes in [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) and the SKILL.md rule on forbidden tools.

66	## Shared Rules
67	
68	These apply regardless of which strategy you use.
69	
70	### Definitions
71	
72	- Every unique `type:typeVersion` pair in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`
73	- Definitions come from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json` — copy the returned node definition object (`Data.Node` or the top-level node object, depending on CLI/plugin version)
74	- **Never hand-write definitions** — hand-written definitions cause validation failures
75	- One definition per unique type, not one per node instance
76	
77	### Layout
78	
79	- Layout (`layout.nodes`, `subflows[<id>].layout`) is owned by `uip maestro flow format` — do not hand-compute coordinates
80	- When authoring a node, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save
81	- Run `uip maestro flow format <file>.flow` after edits and before publish/debug — see [cli-commands.md](../../shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)
82	
83	### Edge rules
84	
85	- `targetPort` is required on every edge — validate rejects edges without it
86	- See [file-format.md — Standard ports](../../shared/file-format.md) for port names by node type
87	- Dynamic ports: decision (`true`/`false`), switch (`case-{id}`/`default`), HTTP (`branch-{id}`/`default`), loop (`output`/`success`/`loopBack`)
88	
89	### Validation
90	
91	- Run `uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json` **once** after all edits complete
92	- Do not validate after each individual edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid
93	- Validation checks: JSON schema, definitions coverage, edge references, unique IDs
94	- Validation does NOT check: connector configuration, connection health, expression correctness, required field completeness
95	
96	### Parallel same-file Edits
97	
98	Applies to any turn that issues more than one `Edit` against the same `.flow` (greenfield T2 and brownfield alike):
99	
100	- **Same-file Edits serialize in execution order** — they do not race, but each later Edit runs against the text the earlier ones already changed. An `old_string` that overlaps text a prior Edit removed or shifted fails with "string not found."
101	- **Anchor each Edit on its target array's OWN opening key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`), located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." Top-level key order and presence are not guaranteed (see [file-format.md](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure)).
102	- **`"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique** — they recur inside inline `definitions[]` and inside any `subflows.<id>` block. Anchor on the 2-space-indented (top-level) occurrence and extend until the match is unique.
103	- Insert at the array's head (right after `[`) so the `old_string` never spans the array's closing `]`.
104	
105	Full per-array anchor table and worked example: [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
106	
107	### Expression prefix rules
108	
109	- Use `=js:` on **value expressions**: end node output `source`, variable updates, HTTP input fields, node `inputs` values
110	- Do NOT use `=js:` on **condition expressions**: decision `expression`, switch case `expression`, HTTP branch `conditionExpression` — these are always evaluated as JS automatically
111	
112	See [variables-and-expressions.md](../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the full expression reference.

No auth required for OOTB nodes; login for tenant-specific connector nodes. 346 347 ```bash 348 uip maestro flow registry pull # refresh local cache (expires after 30 min) 349 uip maestro flow registry list --output json # list all cached node types 350 uip maestro flow registry search --output json # search by name, tag, or category 351 uip maestro flow registry get --output json # get full schema for a node type 352 ``` 353 354 `registry search` returns `Data` as a flat array (not `Data.Nodes`); fields are PascalCase. `NodeType` is the identifier you pass to `registry get ` (and later `node add`). 355 356 ```json 357 { "Data": [ 358 { 359 "NodeType": "uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-sfdc.list-records", 360 "Category": "connector.196536", 361 "DisplayName": "List Records", 362 "Description": "(Salesforce) List records in Salesforce", 363 "Version": "1.0.0", 364 "Tags": "connector, activity", 365 "AvailableOnTenant": true 366 } 367 ] } 368 ``` 369 370 `AvailableOnTenant` is a usability gate, not extra metadata to ignore: 371 372 - `true` — the tenant registry can return this node; it is valid to continue with `registry get ` or `node add `. 373 - `false` — the SDK knows about this node type, but the current tenant registry did not return it. 65:## Filter Trees (CEQL)
66-
67-Some IS activities — most notably **List All Records** and other list/query operations — accept a server-side filter expressed in **CEQL** (Connector Expression Query Language). As with trigger filters (which compile to JMESPath), CEQL filters are authored as a **structured filter tree** and the CLI compiles them to a CEQL string. Authoring as a tree keeps the CLI and Studio Web in lockstep so the activity round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
68-
69-### Contract — three signals from IS metadata
70-
71-The CLI reads the live IS metadata response and uses three signals to wire the filter:
72-
73-1. **The activity supports CEQL** when one of its `parameters` declares `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. That parameter's `name` is the connector-specific key the compiled CEQL string is sent under — most commonly `where`, but **not always** (e.g. Salesforce uses `q`). Activities with no such parameter do not support server-side filtering — pass no `filter` and filter downstream.
74-2. **A field is filterable** when its IS metadata entry has `searchable: true`. Type alone does not gate it — the connector flags fields explicitly. Fields without `searchable: true` are rejected by the CLI even if they look like primitives.
75-3. **Permitted operators** for the field are listed under `searchableOperators`. **Connector-side identifier** for the field in CEQL is `searchableNames[0]` when present (some connectors expose a friendly `name` but require a different identifier in the query string).
76-
77-### What the CLI persists from a single `filter` input
78-
79-- **Runtime side** — the compiled CEQL string lands at `inputs.detail.queryParameters.<filterParamName>` where `<filterParamName>` is the FilterBuilder parameter's name from the IS metadata (often `where`).
80-- **Design-time side** — the structured tree is embedded under `inputs.detail.configuration`'s `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>`. Studio Web reads this on open to re-render the filter widget; without it the filter UI shows up empty even though the runtime call still works.
81-
82-Pass `filter` (the structured tree) and the CLI emits both halves in lockstep. Passing both `filter` and `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` is rejected at validation time — single source of truth.
83-
84-### Tree shape
85-
86-Identical to the trigger filter tree — the same `FilterTree` / `Filter` / `WorkflowValue` types are used; only the compiler output (CEQL vs JMESPath) differs.
87-
88-```jsonc
89-{
90-  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
91-  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
92-  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
93-    {
94-      "id": "<fieldName>",        // resource field name from `is resources describe`
95-      "operator": "<Operator>",   // PascalCase, see operator table below
96-      "value": {
97-        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time / array
98-        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
99-        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not yet supported
100-      }
101-    }
102-  ],
103-  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
104-}
105-```
106-
107-A no-op filter — used when the user wants to list all records without restriction — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
108-
109-### Compiled CEQL output
110-
111-The CLI compiles each leaf to `<field> <op> <value>` (or `<field> <function>` for null checks) and joins siblings with the group operator. String values are wrapped in single quotes; booleans, numerics, and enums are passed bare.
112-
113-| Operator | CEQL token | Notes |
114-|---|---|---|
115-| `Equals` | `=` | |
116-| `NotEquals` | `!=` | |
117-| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | `<` / `<=` / `>` / `>=` | Numeric / date-time |
118-| `Contains` / `NotContains` | `Contains` / `Not Contains` | Substring (string) |
119-| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | `Starts With` / `Not Starts With` / `Ends With` / `Not Ends With` | String |
120-| `Like` / `NotLike` | `Like` / `Not Like` | Pattern match (connector-specific) |
121-| `In` / `NotIn` | `In` / `Not In` | Membership — `value.value` is a list; rendered as `(v1, v2, …)` |
122-| `IsNull` / `IsNotNull` | `Is Null` / `Is Not Null` | No `value` needed |
123-| `Is` / `IsNot` | `=` against literal `true` / `false` | Boolean shortcut |
124-
125-Logical operators between siblings:
126-
127-| `groupOperator` | CEQL token |
128-|---|---|
129-| `0` (And) | ` AND ` |
130-| `1` (Or) | ` OR ` |
131-
132-### Examples
133-
134-**Active accounts only:**
135-
136-```json
137-{
138-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
139-  "filters": [
140-    { "id": "Status", "operator": "Equals",
141-      "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }
142-  ]
143-}
144-```
145-→ CEQL: `Status = 'Active'`
146-
147-**Score ≥ 80 AND Region in (EMEA, APAC):**
148-
149-```json
150-{
151-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
152-  "filters": [
153-    { "id": "Score", "operator": "GreaterThanOrEqual",
154-      "value": { "value": 80, "rawString": "80", "isLiteral": true } },
155-    { "id": "Region", "operator": "In",
156-      "value": { "value": ["EMEA", "APAC"], "rawString": "[\"EMEA\",\"APAC\"]", "isLiteral": true } }
157-  ]
158-}
159-```
160-→ CEQL: `Score >= 80 AND Region In ('EMEA', 'APAC')`
161-
162-**Subject contains "urgent" AND (owner = me OR owner is null):**
163-
164-```json
165-{
166-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
167-  "filters": [
168-    { "id": "Subject", "operator": "Contains",
169-      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
170-  ],
171-  "groups": [
172-    {

It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals).
